The '''2017–18 season''' was '''[[FC Barcelona|Futbol Club Barcelona]]'s''' 119th in existence and the club's [[All-time La Liga table|87th consecutive season]] in the top flight of Spanish football. This was also the first year under head coach [[Ernesto Valverde]].

The team produced a solid season, clinching the [[Double (association football)|domestic double]], going undefeated in the league up until match day 37, where Barça lost to [[Levante UD|Levante]] 4–5, and producing an emphatic 5–0 victory over [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] in the Copa final. However, in the Champions League, Barcelona crashed out in the quarter-finals for the third year in a row, losing to [[A.S. Roma|Roma]] 0–3 and being eliminated on away goals as a result (after a 4–1 home victory). The season was the first since [[2013–14 FC Barcelona season|2013–14 season]] without [[Neymar]], who departed to join [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]].

==Season overview==
===May===
On 29 May, the club announced [[Ernesto Valverde]] would be the new Barcelona coach following the departure of [[Luis Enrique (footballer)|Luis Enrique]] at the end of the previous season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/ernesto-valverde-is-the-new-fc-barcelona-coach |title=Ernesto Valverde is the new FC Barcelona coach. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=29 May 2017 |access-date=29 May 2017}}</ref>

On 29 May, Barcelona and goalkeeper [[Marc-André ter Stegen]] negotiated a five-year contract extension lasting until 30 June 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/fc-barcelona-extends-ter-stegen-contract-with-until-2022 |title=FC Barcelona extends Ter Stegen contract until 2022.|publisher=fcbarcelona.com |access-date=29 May 2017}}</ref>

===June===
On 14 June, [[Fluminense FC|Fluminense]] centre-back [[Marlon (footballer, born September 1995)|Marlon Santos]] signed a three-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/barca-b/news/2016-2017/marlon-santos-to-continue-at-fc-barcelona|title=Marlon Santos to continue at FC Barcelona |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=14 June 2017 |access-date=14 June 2017}}</ref>

On 30 June, goalkeeper [[Jordi Masip]]'s contract expired; he was not resigned and was therefore released.

On 30 June, the club activated a buyback clause for [[Everton F.C.|Everton]]'s [[Gerard Deulofeu]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/signing-fc-barcelona-exercises-their-right-to-buy-gerard-deulofeu-back|title=FC Barcelona exercises their right to buy Gerard Deulofeu back. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=30 June 2017 |access-date=30 June 2017}}</ref>

On 30 June, the club announced they have reached an agreement with [[Real Betis]] for the transfer of [[Cristian Tello]] for €4&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/cristian-tello-completes-transfer-to-real-betis-balompie|title=Cristian Tello completes transfer to Real Betis Balompié. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=30 June 2017 |access-date=30 June 2017}}</ref>

===July===
On 7 July, Barcelona and [[Jérémy Mathieu]] agreed to mutually terminate the defender's contract. Mathieu subsequently joined Portuguese club [[Sporting CP]] on a free transfer.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/jeremy-mathieu-and-fc-barcelona-part-ways |publisher=FCBarcelona.com | title=Jérémy Mathieu and FC Barcelona part ways.|date=7 July 2017 |access-date=5 July 2017}}</ref>

On 13 July, Barcelona and [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] reached an agreement for the transfer of right-back [[Nélson Semedo]] for €30&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/agreement-with-benfica-for-nelson-semedo |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |title=Agreement reached between FC Barcelona and Benfica on Nélson Semedo transfer.|date=13 July 2017 |access-date=13 July 2017}}</ref>

On 21 July, Barcelona defeated [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] 2–1 in a pre-season friendly. [[Neymar]] notched two impeccable first-half goals as the Catalans rolled past the Italian champions before 82,104 fans at a sold-out [[MetLife Stadium]] in the [[2017 International Champions Cup]]. [[Giorgio Chiellini]] pulled one back for Juventus in the 63rd minute, not enough to keep the Ernesto Valverde era from beginning with a convincing win.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-fc-barcelona-2-1-juventus-metlife-stadium-united-states-valverde-neymar-messi |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |title=MATCH REPORT: FC Barcelona opens Valverde era with impressive 2–1 win over Juventus |date=23 July 2017 |access-date=24 July 2017}}</ref>

On 26 July, Barcelona won 1–0 against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] in a pre-season friendly. Neymar scored in the 31st minute.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-fc-barcelona-victory-manchester-united-international-champions-cup-washington-dc-united-states-neymar |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |title=FC Barcelona beat Manchester United by the minimum in second stop on US tour |date=27 July 2017 |access-date=27 July 2017}}</ref>

On 29 July, Barcelona defeated [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]] 3–2 in their final match of the U.S. tour, winning the United States edition of the 2017 International Champions Cup. Messi, [[Ivan Rakitić]] and [[Gerard Piqué]] each scored one goal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-classic-american-dream-in-miami-fc-barcelona-real-madrid |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |title=MATCH REPORT: Classic American dream in Miami! |date=29 July 2017 |access-date=29 July 2017}}</ref>

===August===
On 3 August, Barcelona confirmed the unilateral termination of Neymar's contract as Neymar's legal representatives paid his €222&nbsp;million [[buyout clause]]. In turn, Barcelona announced a turnover of operation details to [[UEFA]] so as to allow UEFA to determine any disciplinary responsibilities that may arise.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/fc-barcelona-communique-on-neymar-jr-buyout-clause |title=FC Barcelona communique on Neymar Jr |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=3 August 2017 |access-date=3 August 2017}}</ref> Neymar subsequently joined [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] on a five-year contract.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://en.psg.fr/pro/article/neymar-jr-signs-with-paris-saint-germain |title=Neymar Jr signs with Paris Saint-Germain |publisher=PSG |date=3 August 2017 |access-date=3 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170803205243/https://en.psg.fr/pro/article/neymar-jr-signs-with-paris-saint-germain |archive-date=3 August 2017 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref>

On 4 August, Barcelona drew 1–1 with [[Gimnàstic de Tarragona|Gimnàstic]] in a pre-season friendly game in [[Tarragona]]. [[Manu Barreiro]] put the hosts ahead in the 11th minute only for [[Paco Alcácer]] to score the equalizer for the ''Blaugrana'' from a [[Direct free kick|free-kick]] in the 79th minute.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-nastic-de-tarragona-fc-barcelona-still-unbeaten-draw-1-1-|title=Nàstic Tarragona 1-1 FC Barcelona: A draw to remain unbeaten|date=4 August 2017|website=FCBarcelona.com|access-date=6 August 2017}}</ref>

On 7 August, Barcelona defeated [[Associação Chapecoense de Futebol|Chapecoense]] 5–0 in the [[2017 Joan Gamper Trophy|52nd edition]] of the [[Joan Gamper Trophy]]. Gerard Deulofeu, Sergio Busquets, Messi, [[Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)|Luis Suárez]] and [[Denis Suárez]] were the scorers for ''Barça''; Messi and Deulofeu also assisted two goals each. Busquets was named the [[Man of the Match]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/gamper-match-report-fc-barcelona-5-0-chapecoense-football-is-the-winner|title=FC Barcelona 5-0 Chapecoense: Football is the winner|date=7 August 2017|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|access-date=7 August 2017}}</ref>

On 13 August, Barcelona lost 1–3 to Real Madrid in the first leg of the [[2017 Supercopa de España]]. The first half of the match ended goalless. Five minutes into the second half, [[Marcelo (footballer, born 1988)|Marcelo]] fired a cross that deflected off Piqué's foot, resulting in an [[own goal#Association football|own goal]]. In the 77th minute, Luis Suárez was brought down in the box by goalkeeper [[Keylor Navas]], resulting in a penalty which was converted by Lionel Messi. Messi's hit marked his 25th goal in the fixture.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/social-networks-leo-messi-and-luis-suarez-call-for-optimism|title=Leo Messi and Luis Suárez call for optimism|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=14 August 2017|access-date=16 August 2017}}</ref> In the 80th minute, Real Madrid scored their second through a counterattack when [[Isco]] assisted [[Cristiano Ronaldo]], who shot into the top right corner from the edge of the box. Ronaldo was booked for removing his shirt as part of his celebrations. Two minutes later, he was booked again for a [[Diving (association football)|dive]] in the penalty box, which resulted in a [[red card (football)|red card]] and a subsequent suspension for the second leg. Real's last goal was scored in the 90th minute in similar fashion to the second, when [[Marco Asensio]] shot into the top left corner following an assist from [[Lucas Vázquez]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-fc-barcelona-1-3-real-madrid-to-be-continued... |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |title=FC Barcelona 1-3 Real Madrid: To be continued... |date=13 August 2017 |access-date=13 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171029152757/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-fc-barcelona-1-3-real-madrid-to-be-continued... |archive-date=29 October 2017 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref>

On 14 August, Barcelona announced they had reached an agreement with [[Guangzhou Evergrande Taobao F.C.|Guangzhou Evergrande Taobao]] for the transfer of [[Paulinho (footballer, born July 1988)|Paulinho]] for €40&nbsp;million. His release clause was set at €120&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/paulinho-bezerra-fc-barcelona-s-new-signing |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |title=Paulinho Bezerra, FC Barcelona's new signing |date=14 August 2017 |access-date=14 August 2017}}</ref>

On 16 August, Barcelona lost 2–0 ([[aggregate score|agg.]] 1–5) to Real Madrid in the second leg of the 2017 Supercopa de España. The first goal of the match came quite early through a Real throw-in the fourth minute which resulted into getting the ball to Marco Asensio, who scored from long range. Nine minutes after the half-hour mark, Marcelo crossed in for [[Karim Benzema]] to control, who finished it with a half-volley into the net which was enough for the win for Real.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-real-madrid-2-0-fc-barcelona-super-cup-slips-away|title=Real Madrid 2-0 FC Barcelona: Super Cup slips away|publisher=FC Barcelona.com|language=en-US|access-date=2017-08-17}}</ref>

On 20 August, Barcelona defeated Real Betis 2–0 in their first Liga match of the season, following an own goal from [[Alin Toșca]] and a second within three minutes by [[Sergi Roberto]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-fc-barcelona-real-betis-2-0-opening-win-la-liga |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |title=MATCH REPORT: Barça ease past Betis to claim 2-0 win |date=20 August 2017 |access-date=20 August 2017}}</ref>

On 24 August, Barcelona confirmed the transfer of [[Sergi Samper]] to [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/agreement-with-ud-las-palmas-for-loan-of-sergi-samper|title=Agreement with UD Las Palmas for loan of Sergi Samper {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-08-24}}</ref>

On 25 August, Barcelona announced they had reached an agreement with [[Borussia Dortmund]] for the transfer of [[Ousmane Dembélé]] for €105&nbsp;million plus add-ons. The player signed a five-year contract and his [[buyout clause]] was set at €400&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/press-release-ousmane-dembele-fcbarcelona-signing |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |title=Ousmane Dembélé, FC Barcelona's new signing|date=25 August 2017 |access-date=25 August 2017}}</ref>

On 26 August, Barcelona defeated [[Deportivo Alavés|Alavés]] 0–2 at [[Mendizorrotza Stadium|Mendizorrotza]]. [[Lionel Messi|Messi]] scored both goals, although having a penalty saved by [[Fernando Pacheco Flores|Pacheco]]. [[Paulinho (footballer, born July 1988)|Paulinho]] made his debut for Barcelona.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-alaves-fc-barcelona-messi-at-the-double-0-2-|title=[MATCH REPORT] Alavés 0–2 FC Barcelona: Messi helps Barça to two out of two {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-08-26}}</ref>

On 29 August, [[OGC Nice|Nice]] and Barcelona reached an agreement for the loan of [[Marlon (footballer, born September 1995)|Marlon]] for two years, with a buy-back option for Barcelona after the first year.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/agreement-between-nice-and-fc-barcelona-for-the-loan-of-marlon-santos|title=Loan agreement with Nice for Marlon Santos {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-08-30}}</ref>

On 31 August, Barcelona and [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] reached an agreement for the loan of [[Douglas (footballer, born August 1990)|Douglas]] until the end of the 2017–18 campaign.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/douglas-loaned-to-benfica|title=Agreement with Benfica for the loan of Douglas {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-08-31}}</ref>

===September===
On 1 September, Barcelona and [[Deportivo Alavés|Alavés]] reached an agreement for the loan of [[Munir El Haddadi|Munir]] until the end of the 2017–18 campaign.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/agreement-alaves-munir-loan|title=Club reach agreement for Munir's loan move to Alavés {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-09-01}}</ref>

On 5 September, midfielder [[Carles Aleñá]] signed a new contract, keeping him at the club for a further three years with an optional extra two years.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/carles-alena-signs-contract-extension|title=Carles Aleñá signs contract extension {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-09-06}}</ref>

On 9 September, Barcelona defeated [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] 5–0 in the [[Derbi barceloní]]. [[Lionel Messi|Messi]] scored a hat-trick while [[Gerard Piqué|Piqué]] and [[Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)|Suárez]] topped off the scoring. [[Ousmane Dembélé]] made his debut, coming on as a substitute for [[Gerard Deulofeu]] in the 68th minute; he set Suárez up for the final goal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-fc-barcelona-5-0-rcd-espanyol-derby-delight|title=FC Barcelona 5-0 RCD Espanyol: Derby delight {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-09-09}}</ref>

On 12 September, Barcelona beat [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] 3–0 in their first game of the [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League]], following a brace by Messi and another goal by Rakitić.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-barca-3-0-juventus-mamma-mia-|title=Barça 3-0 Juventus: Mamma mia! {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-09-12}}</ref>

On 16 September, Barcelona defeated [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] 1–2 in a hard-fought game at the [[Coliseum Alfonso Pérez]]. [[Gaku Shibasaki|Shibasaki]] scored a stunning goal for Getafe in the first half while both of Barcelona's goals came in the second half from substitutes [[Denis Suárez]] and [[Paulinho (footballer, born July 1988)|Paulinho]], the latter of whom scored his maiden Barcelona goal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-getafe-1-2-fc-barcelona-super-subs-do-the-job|title=[MATCH REPORT] Getafe 1-2 Barça: Super subs do the job {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-09-16}}</ref>

On 19 September, Barcelona defeated [[SD Eibar|Eibar]] 6–1, with Messi scoring four and Paulinho and Denis Suárez getting the other goals. Eibar's only goal was scored by [[Sergi Enrich]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-fc-barcelona-6-eibar-1-la-liga|title=MATCH REPORT FC Barcelona – SD Eibar: Six of the best {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-09-19}}</ref>

On 23 September, Barcelona defeated [[Girona Futbol Club|Girona]] 0–3 in their first ever Catalan derby. Girona captain [[Aday Benítez|Aday]] and goalkeeper [[Gorka Iraizoz|Iraizoz]] inadvertently steered the ball into their own net to give Barcelona a two-goal lead, before Luis Suárez topped off the scoring.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-girona-fc-0-3-fc-barcelona-top-cats|title=Girona FC 0-3 FC Barcelona: Top cats {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-09-23}}</ref>

On 27 September, Barcelona defeated [[Sporting CP|Sporting Lisbon]] 0–1 on the 2nd matchday of the Champions League, at the [[Estádio José Alvalade]]. Barça were dependent on a lone own goal by [[Sebastián Coates]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-sporting-clube-portugal-0-1-fc-barcelona-lions-tamed-in-lisbon|title=Sporting Clube Portugal 0-1 FC Barcelona: Lions tamed in Lisbon {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-09-27}}</ref>

===October===
On 1 October, Barcelona defeated [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]] 3–0 in a game played behind closed doors at the Camp Nou, due to violence in [[Catalonia]] relating to an [[2017 Catalan independence referendum|ongoing independence referendum]]. Sergio Busquets scored through a header, while Messi topped off the scoring with a brace.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-fc-barcelona-las-palmas-a-victory-in-silence-3-0-|title=[MATCH REPORT] FC Barcelona 3-0 Las Palmas: Victory at an empty Camp Nou {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-10-01}}</ref> Prior to the game, two directors, Jordi Monés and Carles Vilarrubí, handed in their resignations in protest to the game being played.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/club/news/2017-2018/institutional-statement-by-fc-barcelona-president-josep-maria-bartomeu|title=Institutional statement by Josep Maria Bartomeu {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-10-03}}</ref>

On 3 October, Barcelona joined the country-wide strike called by ‘Taula per la Democràcia’ (Table for Democracy) and therefore the club offices remained closed. None of the professional teams nor the youth teams at FC Barcelona trained. The Tour Camp Nou Experience and the Museum as well as the OAB were also closed.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/fc-barcelona-closed-october-3|title=FC Barcelona closed 3 October {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-10-03}}</ref>

On 6 October, midfielder [[Andrés Iniesta]] signed a lifetime contract with Barcelona, keeping him with the club for the remainder of his career.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/andres-iniesta-to-sign-deal-to-stay-at-fc-barcelona-for-life|title=Andrés Iniesta signs lifetime contract with FC Barcelona {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-10-06}}</ref>

On 14 October, Barcelona were held by [[Atlético Madrid]] to a 1–1 draw at the [[Metropolitano Stadium|Wanda Metropolitano]], which effectively ended their winning streak. [[Saúl Ñíguez|Saúl]] scored early into the game to give Atlético the lead, but [[Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)|Luis Suárez]] saved Barça's day with a last-gasp header.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-atletico-madrid-1-1-fc-barcelona-still-undefeated|title=[MATCH REPORT] Atlético Madrid 1–1 FC Barcelona: Still undefeated {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-10-14}}</ref>

On 18 October, Barcelona won against [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]] 3–1 at home. The Catalans maintained a perfect start thanks to an early own-goal, Messi's 100th European goal, and one from Digne, although the visitors did pull one back at the last minute. Barcelona had a goal ruled for offside and one deemed to have touched Piqué's hand and entered the net, resulting in his second yellow of the night, and his suspension for the return game.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-fc-barcelona-3-1-olympiacos-barca-pass-greek-test-3-1-|title=FC Barcelona v Olympiacos: Barça pass Greek test (3-1) {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-10-18}}</ref>

On 21 October, table-toppers Barcelona defeated winless [[Málaga CF|Málaga]] 2–0 at home. Deulofeu controversially grabbed an early goal, while Iniesta added a second later in the final half.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-fc-barcelona-2-0-malaga-win-maintains-100-home-record|title=FC Barcelona 2-0 Málaga: Win maintains 100% home record {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-10-21}}</ref>

On 24 October, Barcelona defeated [[Real Murcia]] 3–0 in their [[2017–18 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]] opener. [[Paco Alcácer]] scored a header just before the break, while Deulofeu scored in the second half and [[FC Barcelona B|Barça B]] youngster [[José Arnaiz]] quickly added the third on his debut with the first team.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-barca-3-0-real-murcia-copa-del-rey-last-32|title=Match Report: Plenty in Reserve {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-10-24}}</ref>

On 28 October, Barcelona won against [[Athletic Bilbao]] 0–2 away at the [[San Mamés Stadium (2013)|Nuevo San Mamés]]. Goals from Messi and Paulinho split the teams in Bilbao to ensure the Catalans stay four points clear at the top of the Liga table.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/athletic-club-0-2-fc-barcelona-survival-at-san-mames|title=Match Report: Athletic Club 0-2 FC Barcelona: Survival at San Mamés {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-10-28}}</ref>

On 31 October, Barcelona were held by Olympiacos to a goal-less draw at the [[Karaiskakis Stadium]] in [[Piraeus]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-olympiacos-0-0-fc-barcelona-shutout-in-piraeus|title=Olympiacos 0-0 FC Barcelona: Shutout in Piraeus {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-10-31}}</ref>

===November===
On 4 November, Barcelona defeated [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] at a rainy night at the Camp Nou. [[Paco Alcácer]] opened the scoring with a goal early in the game, while [[Guido Pizarro|Pizarro]] headed in the equaliser in the second half, Alcácer netted his second and also the match deciding goal few minutes later.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-fc-barcelona-sevilla-alcacer-at-the-double-2-1-|title=FC Barcelona- Sevilla: Alcácer at the double (2-1) {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-11-04}}</ref>

On 18 November, Barcelona won against [[CD Leganés|Leganés]] 0–3 at the [[Estadio Municipal de Butarque]]. Suárez ended his 5-game goalless streak with two strikes from rebounds, while Paulinho added the final touch. Piqué received his 5th yellow card of the season, meaning he misses Barça's next match.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-leganes-0-2-fcbarcelona-super-suarez-strikes-twice|title=MATCH REPORT: Leganés 0-3 Barça: Super Suárez strikes twice {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-11-19}}</ref>

On 22 November, Barcelona were held to a 0–0 draw against [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] at the [[Juventus Stadium|Allianz Stadium]], thereby qualifying for the Round of 16 of the Champions League.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-recap-juventus-fc-fc-barcelona-0-0-draw-tie-last-16-group-d-winners|title=MATCH REPORT: Scoreless draw at Juventus sends Barça to last 16 as group winners {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-11-22}}</ref>

On 25 November, Messi signed a new deal with Barcelona, keeping him with the club till the end of the 2020/21 season. His buyout clause was set at €700 million.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/video-lionel-messi-signs-new-contract-fc-barcelona|title=Lionel Messi signs new deal through 2020/21 season {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-11-25}}</ref>

On 26 November, Barcelona tied with [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] at the [[Mestalla Stadium]]. A Messi shot was dropped into the goal by [[Neto (footballer, born 1989)|Neto]], but was disallowed by the referee. In the second half, [[Rodrigo (footballer, born 1991)|Rodrigo]] put Valencia in the lead, but [[Jordi Alba]] scored through a Messi assist in the dying minutes.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-valencia-1-1-fc-barcelona-entertaining-point-la-liga-13th-fixture-2017-18|title=Match Report: Valencia 1-1 FC Barcelona: Entertaining point in Mestalla {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-11-26}}</ref>

On 29 November, Barcelona thrashed Real Murcia 5–0 ([[Aggregate score|agg.]] 8–0) at the Camp Nou. Paco Alcácer, Piqué, [[Aleix Vidal]], Denis Suárez and José Arnaiz, were the scorers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-recap-fc-barcelona-5-0-murcia-copa-del-rey-victory-last-16-video-highlights|title=MATCH REPORT: Barça sails past Murcia, 5–0, and into the last 16 of the Copa del Rey {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-11-29}}</ref>

===December===
On 2 December, Barcelona were held to a 2–2 draw by [[Celta Vigo]] at the Camp Nou. [[Iago Aspas]] scored at the 20-minute mark, but Messi equalized within a few minutes. Luis Suárez put Barça in the lead in the second half, but again, the score was equalized by [[Maxi Gómez]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-fc-barcelona-celta-cold-comfort-2-2-|title=FC Barcelona vs Celta: Cold Comfort (2-2) {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-12-02}}</ref>

On 5 December, Barcelona defeated Sporting Lisbon 2–0, with a goal from a Paco Alcácer header, and an own goal from ex-Barça player [[Jérémy Mathieu]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-recap-fc-barcelona-sporting-clube-portugal-2-0-victory-uefa-champions-league-group-d|title=MATCH REPORT: Barça use winning formula to wrap up group play with 2–0 win over Sporting Clube {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-12-06}}</ref>

On 10 December, Barcelona won against [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] 0–2 at [[Estadio de la Cerámica]]. Both goals came late into the game, with one each scored by Messi and Suárez. Villarreal's [[Dani Raba|Raba]] got a direct red for a challenge on Sergio.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-villarreal-fc-barcelona-a-victory-in-style-0-2|title=Villarreal v FC Barcelona: A victory in style (0-2) {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-12-10}}</ref> Messi's goal equalled the record in Europe's major leagues of the Bayern Munich striker [[Gerd Müller]] with 525 goals with one club.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/messi-equals-gerd-muller-fcbarcelona|title=Messi equals Gerd Müller {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-12-10}}</ref>

On 17 December, Barcelona won against La Coruña 4–0, Suárez and Paulinho scored two goals each.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-fc-barcelona-4-0-deportivo-winter-wonderland|title=FC Barcelona 4-0 Deportivo: Winter wonderland {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-12-17}}</ref>

On 23 December, Barcelona defeated Real Madrid 0–3 at the Bernabéu. Suárez, Messi and Aleix Vidal each scored a goal that saw the Blaugrana head into the Christmas break 14 points clear of the defending champions.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/real-madrid-0-fcbarcelona-3-messi-christmas-match-report|title=Real Madrid 0 Barça 3: Messi Christmas! {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2017-12-23}}</ref>

===January===
On 4 January, Barcelona were held to a 1–1 draw by Celta Vigo. A gripping cup first leg ended at Balaídos all square on the night that Ousmane Dembélé made his long-awaited return from injury.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-celta-1-1-fc-barcelona-nothing-decided|title=Celta 1–1 FC Barcelona: Nothing decided {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-01-04}}</ref>

On 6 January, Barcelona announced that they had reached an agreement with [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] for the transfer of [[Philippe Coutinho]]. The player signed a contract for the remainder of the season and five more, and has a buyout clause of €400 million.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/philippe-coutinho-new-player-fc-barcelona|title=Philippe Coutinho, new FC Barcelona player {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-01-06}}</ref>

On 7 January, Barcelona won against Levante 3–0, Ernesto Valverde's men kicked off the New Year in La Liga with an impressive team performance and goals from Messi, Suárez and Paulinho.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-fc-barcelona-v-levante-ud-first-three-points-of-2018-3-0-|title=Match Report: FC Barcelona v Levante UD: First three points of 2018 (3–0) {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-01-07}}</ref>

On 11 January, Barcelona and [[Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras]] reached an agreement for the transfer of [[Yerry Mina]] for the remainder of the season and five more until June 30, 2023. The cost of the transfer was €11.8 million and his release clause was set at €100 million.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/agreement-for-the-transfer-of-yerry-mina-palmeiras-fc-barcelona|title=Agreement for the transfer of Yerry Mina {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-01-11}}</ref>

On 11 January, Barcelona defeated Celta Vigo 5–0 (agg. 6–1) at the Camp Nou. Four goals in the first 31 minutes (2 from Messi and one each from Jordi Alba and Luis Suárez) got the job done early and Rakitic headed in a late fifth as the Catalans cruised into the quarter-finals of the Copa del Rey.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-copa-del-rey-barca-5-0-celta-quick-off-the-mark|title=Barça 5-0 Celta: Quick off the mark {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-01-11}}</ref>

On 13 January, Barcelona and [[İstanbul Başakşehir F.K.]] agreed on a loan deal for Turkish midfielder [[Arda Turan]] for the remainder of the season and two more.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/communique-agreement-with-istanbul-basaksehir-fk-for-the-loan-of-arda-turan|title=Agreement with Istanbul Basaksehir FK for the loan of Arda Turan {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-01-13}}</ref>

On 14 January, Barcelona defeated [[Real Sociedad]] away at the [[Estadio Anoeta|Anoeta Stadium]] with a score of 2–4. This was the first time Barça beat La Real away since May 2007. Barça were 2–0 down at the 35th minute, until Paulinho scored Barça's first in the 39th minute. Suárez scored in the 50th and 71st minute, and Messi scored a [[free kick]] in the 85th minute to complete the comeback.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-real-sociedad-v-fc-barcelona-thrilling-comeback-win-4-2-suarez|title=MATCH REPORT: Real Sociedad v FC Barcelona: Thrilling comeback win (2-4) {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-01-14}}</ref>

On 17 January, Barcelona was defeated by Espanyol 1–0 away. Barça dominated in Cornellà but failed to find the net as the home side snatched a winner three minutes from the end.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-rcd-espanyol-1-0-fc-barcelona-derby-defeat|title=RCD Espanyol 1-0 FC Barcelona: Derby defeat {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-01-17}}</ref>

On 19 January, Barcelona and Sergi Roberto reached an agreement to renew his contract through to 30 June 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/roberto-contract-renewal-fc-barcelona-2022|title=Sergi Roberto and FC Barcelona agree contract renewal through to 2022 {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-01-19}}</ref>

On 21 January, Barcelona beat Real Betis 0–5 away at the [[Estadio Benito Villamarín]]. Valverde's men won in style with five second-half goals within 30 minutes as Rakitic, Messi (2), and Suárez (2) all found the net.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-real-betis-v-fc-barcelona-sensational-second-half-5-0-|title=Real Betis v FC Barcelona: Sensational second half (5-0) {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-01-21}}</ref>

On 22 January, Barcelona announced that they had reached an agreement with [[Inter Milan]] for the loan of [[Rafinha (footballer, born February 1993)|Rafinha]] until 30 June 2018. Inter has an option to purchase the player for €35M+€3M euros in variables, which must be confirmed before the end of the current season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/agreement-with-inter-milan-for-the-loan-of-rafinha-fcbarcelona|title=Agreement with Inter Milan for the loan of Rafinha {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-01-22}}</ref>

On 25 January, Barcelona defeated Espanyol 2–0 ([[Aggregate score|agg. 2–1]]) at home. Philippe Coutinho's debut, and goals from Lionel Messi and Luis Suárez brought the Camp Nou to its feet as Barça reached the semi-finals of the Copa del Rey.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-fc-barcelona-v-espanyol-derby-delight-2-0-|title=FC Barcelona v Espanyol: Derby delight (2-0) {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-01-25}}</ref>

On 28 January, Barcelona beat Alavés 2–1 at home. Barça equaled a club record by going unbeaten in first 21 league games of the season thanks to a second half comeback win with goals from Suárez and Messi.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-fc-barcelona-v-deportivo-alaves-blaugranas-dig-deep-2-1-|title=FC Barcelona v Deportivo Alavés: Blaugranes dig deep (2-1) {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-01-28}}</ref>

On 29 January, Gerard Piqué renewed his contract through to 30 June 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/gerard-pique-signing-contract-renewal-monday-fc-barcelona|title=Gerard Piqué will sign his new contract on Monday {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-01-27}}</ref>

===February===
On 1 February, Barcelona defeated Valencia 1–0 at the Camp Nou. A Luis Suárez header broke the deadlock in a frustrating encounter.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/copa-del-rey-first-leg-semi-final-fc-barcelona-1-0-valencia-in-the-driving-seat|title=FC Barcelona 1-0 Valencia: In the driving seat {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-02-01}}</ref>

On 4 February, Barcelona were held by Espanyol to a 1–1 draw away at the [[RCDE Stadium]]. [[Gerard Moreno (footballer)|Gerard Moreno]]'s opener was cancelled out by a towering header from Gerard Piqué in a torrential downpour.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-rcd-espanyol-fc-barcelona-1-1-pique-all-square-in-the-rain|title=RCD Espanyol – FC Barcelona: All square in the rain (1-1) {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-02-04}}</ref> This draw marked the 22nd consecutive unbeaten game in the league for Barcelona, which is a new club record, beating the previous record of 21 games under [[Pep Guardiola]] in the [[2009–10 FC Barcelona season|2009–10]] season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/best-unbeaten-start-to-a-season-in-la-liga-fcbarcelona|title=Best unbeaten start to a season in La Liga {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-02-05}}</ref>

On 8 February, Barcelona defeated Valencia 0–2 (0-3 on aggregate) at the Mestalla. Coutinho claimed first goal in a blaugrana jersey and Rakitic added a second to send the Catalans into the Copa del Rey final against Sevilla on April 21<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/copa-del-rey-semi-final-second-leg-match-report-valencia-0-2-fc-barcelona-0-3-on-aggregate-|title=Valencia 0-2 FC Barcelona (0-3 on aggregate): Cup finalists once again! {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-02-08}}</ref>

On 11 February, Barcelona drew with Getafe 0–0 at the Camp Nou. The Blaugranas couldn't break down the team from Madrid's resolute defending in a hard-fought game with few clear-cut chances.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-fc-barcelona-v-getafe-cf-a-frustrating-point-0-0-|title=FC Barcelona v Getafe CF: A frustrating point (0-0) {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-02-11}}</ref>

On 17 February, Barcelona beat Eibar 0–2 at [[Ipurua Municipal Stadium|Ipurua]]. Goals from Luis Suárez and Jordi Alba secured three hard-earned points in the Basque Country to match the Club record unbeaten run in La Liga.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/liga-match-report-eibar-0-2-barca-anything-but-easy|title=Eibar 0-2 Barça: Anything but easy {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-02-17}}</ref>

On 20 February, Barcelona drew with Chelsea 1–1 at Stamford Bridge. Iniesta-Messi connection canceled out Willian's opener to set up an enticing second leg at Camp Nou in three weeks' time.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/chelsea-fc-1-1-fc-barcelona-all-square-at-the-bridge-match-report-messi-iniesta|title=Chelsea FC 1-1 FC Barcelona: All square at the Bridge {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-02-20}}</ref>

On 24 February, Barcelona defeated Girona 6–1 at the Camp Nou. A hat-trick from Suárez, two goals from Messi, plus a Coutinho special helped Barça to gain a win.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-barca-girona-unstoppable-6-1-|title=FC Barcelona - Girona: Unstoppable! (6-1) {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-02-25}}</ref>

===March===
On 1 March, Barcelona were held by Las Palmas to a 1–1 draw away from home. A wondrous Messi free kick puts the Catalans in command but the Islanders leveled up from the spot.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-las-palmas-1-1-fc-barcelona-held-in-the-canaries|title=Las Palmas 1-1 FC Barcelona: Held in the Canaries {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-03-01}}</ref>

On 4 March, Barcelona won against Atlético Madrid 1–0 at home. Another Lionel Messi special was enough for Barça to see off determined opponents who fought for the win right to the very end.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-fc-barcelona-atletico-madrid-a-step-closer-1-0-|title=FC Barcelona - Atlético Madrid: A step closer (1-0) {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-03-04}}</ref>

On 7 March, Barcelona defeated Espanyol at the [[Camp d'Esports]] in [[Lleida]]. The third edition of the [[Supercopa de Catalunya]] went down to penalties in Lleida, and the Blaugrana made no mistake and brought the trophy home.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/catalan-super-cup-final-match-report-fc-barcelona-0-0-4-2-on-pens-rcd-espanyol-spot-on-|title=FC Barcelona 0-0 (4-2 on pens) RCD Espanyol: Spot on! {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-03-07}}</ref>

On 10 March, Barcelona won against Málaga 0–2 away. Fabulous first half goals from Suárez and Coutinho were enough to secure a comfortable victory in a top-against-bottom clash.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-malaga-cf-0-2-fc-barcelona-still-going-strong|title=Málaga CF 0-2 FC Barcelona: Still going strong {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-03-10}}</ref>

On 11 March, FC Barcelona confirmed that an agreement had been reached with [[Grêmio Foot-Ball Porto Alegrense|Grêmio]] for the purchase option of Brazilian midfielder [[Arthur Melo|Arthur]]. If Barcelona exercises the option in July 2018, the transfer will cost €30m plus €9m in added variables.<ref>{{cite web|title=Barça and Gremio reach agreement on option for Arthur transfer|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/agreement-signing-option-rights-fc-barcelona-arthur-gremio-brazil-porto-alegre|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=March 2018|access-date=11 March 2018}}</ref>

On 14 March, Barcelona won against Chelsea 3–0 (agg. 4–1). Dembélé notched his debut goal and Messi scored his 99th and 100th career Champions League goals as Barça went through to the last eight for a record-extending 11th straight season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/video-match-report-messi-masters-chelsea-as-fc-barcelona-win-3-0-4-1-agg-and-move-on-to-quarterfinals-uefa-champions-league|title=Match Report: Messi masters Chelsea as FC Barcelona wins, 3–0 (4–1 agg.), and moves on to the Champions League quarterfinals {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-03-14}}</ref>

On 18 March, Barcelona defeated Athletic Bilbao 2–0 at the Camp Nou. A scintillating first-half display from the Blaugranes secured a comfortable 2–0 win with goals from Alcácer and Messi at the Camp Nou.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-fc-fc-barcelona-v-athletic-club-leaders-march-on-2-0-29-la-liga-camp-nou|title=MFC Barcelona v Athletic Club: Leaders march on (2-0) {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-03-18}}</ref>

On 31 March, Barcelona recorded a heart-stopping 2–2 draw at the Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán. Two late goals from Luis Suárez and Lionel Messi earned a draw for Barça after Sevilla had opened up a two-goal lead through Franco Vázquez and Luis Muriel.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-sevilla-fc-fc-barcelona-a-minute-of-magic-2-2-|title=Sevilla FC - FC Barcelona: A minute of magic (2-2) {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-03-31}}</ref>

===April===
On 4 April, Barça took a 4–1 aggregate lead into the second leg after two own goals by Roma and a third from Gerard Piqué; Edin Dzeko answered for Roma before Luis Suárez added some late insurance.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-fc-barcelona-4-1-as-roma-uefa-champions-league-quarterfinals-first-leg-camp-nou-video|title=MATCH REPORT: Barça rolls over Roma, 4–1, as defenders take center stage {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-04-04}}</ref>

On 7 April, Barca defeated Leganes 3–1 drawing level with the joint-record of 38 unbeaten games set by [[Real Sociedad]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/fc-barcelona-equal-real-sociedad-s-unbeaten-record|title=FC Barcelona equal Real Sociedad's unbeaten record {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-04-07}}</ref> thanks to a Messi hat-trick.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/messi-unbeaten-record-match-report-fc-barcelona-3-1-cd-leganes-and-so-it-continues-|title=FC Barcelona 3-1 CD Leganés: And so it continues… {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-04-07}}</ref>

On 10 April, Barça lost 3–0 to Roma. Goals from [[Edin Džeko|Džeko]], [[Daniele De Rossi|De Rossi]] and [[Kostas Manolas|Manolas]] allowed the Italians to turn around a three-goal deficit and qualify for the semi-finals on the away goals rule.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-as-roma-3-0-fc-barcelona-goodbye-to-the-champions-league|title=AS Roma 3-0 FC Barcelona: Goodbye to the Champions League {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-04-10}}</ref>

On 14 April, Barca defeated València 2–1 with goals from Luis Suárez and Samuel Umtiti that secured the longest unbeaten streak (39) in La Liga history.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-fc-barcelona-2-1-valencia-cf-record-breakers|title=FC Barcelona 2-1 València CF: Record breakers {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-04-14}}</ref>

On 17 April, ten-man Barça held on for a 2–2 draw with Celta Vigo at Balaídos. Ousmane Dembélé scored his first La Liga goal and Paco Alcácer got the other. Sergi Roberto was sent off in the 71st minute but Barca held on to remain unbeaten in the league.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-celta-vigo-fc-barcelona-all-square-in-galicia-2-2-|title=Celta Vigo – FC Barcelona: All square in Galicia (2-2) {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-04-17}}</ref>

On 21 April, Barcelona cruised to their fourth consecutive Copa del Rey title as they beat Sevilla 5–0 at the Wanda Metropolitano. The goals were scored by Luis Suarez (2), Messi, Iniesta and Coutinho.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/copa-del-rey-final-match-report-sevilla-0-5-fc-barcelona-wanda-ful-|title=Sevilla 0-5 FC Barcelona: Wanda-ful! {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-04-21}}</ref>

On 27 April, [[Andrés Iniesta]] announced that he would be leaving the club at the end of the season after 22 incredible years. Iniesta, a World Cup winner with Spain, won nine La Liga titles alongside four Champions League wins and six Copa del Rey crowns.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/andres-iniesta-fc-barcelona-press-news-conference|title=Andrés Iniesta announces his Barça goodbye {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-04-27}}</ref>

On 29 April, Barcelona defeated Deportivo La Coruna 4–2 to win their 25th La Liga title. Coutinho scored the opening goal before Messi sealed the title with a hat trick.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-deportivo-2-4-fc-barcelona-liga-champions-|title=Deportivo 2-4 FC Barcelona: Liga champions! {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-04-29}}</ref>

===May===
On 6 May, 10-man Barcelona held on for a dramatic 2–2 draw in El Clasico against Real Madrid to extend their unbeaten streak in the league. Luis Suarez and Leo Messi scored the goals for Barca which were cancelled out by goals from Cristiano Ronaldo and Gareth Bale. Sergi Roberto was sent off in first-half injury time following an altercation with Marcelo.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-fc-barcelona-vs-real-madrid-still-undefeated-2-2-|title=MATCH REPORT: Barça and Real Madrid draw 2-2, as Catalans extend unbeaten streak {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-05-06}}</ref>

On 9 May, a much changed Barcelona side defeated Villarreal 5–1. Barca's new signings Coutinho, Paulinho and Dembele (2) were all on target with Messi getting the other goal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-barca-5-1-villarreal-champagne-football|title=Barça 5-1 Villarreal: Champagne football {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-05-09}}</ref>

On 13 May, Barcelona's unbeaten run came to the end when they lost to Levante 4–5. Barcelona mounted a spirited comeback after trailing 1–5 but fell agonizingly short. The only bright spot in the game was a hat-trick by Philippe Coutinho. The other goal was scored by Luis Suarez from the penalty spot.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-levante-ud-v-fc-barcelona-undefeated-run-comes-to-end-5-4-|title=Levante UD v FC Barcelona: Undefeated run comes to end (5–4) {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-05-13}}</ref>

On 20 May, Barcelona defeated Real Sociedad 1–0 in Iniesta's final game as a Barcelona player. The only goal of the game was a breathtaking strike from Iniesta's heir apparent – Coutinho. Iniesta received a standing ovation from the Camp Nou when he was substituted in the 82nd minute. This game also marked the last appearance for Real Sociedad legend Xabi Prieto.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-fc-barcelona-v-real-sociedad-win-for-infinite-iniesta-1-0-|title=MATCH REPORT: FC Barcelona v Real Sociedad: Win for Infinite Iniesta (1-0) {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=2018-05-20}}</ref>
